chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We send dirhams with an exchange rate to Ahwaz, so goods are bought for us with them. Then we wait. When they are sold, the exchange rate is placed against them. So when we sell them, is it upon us to mention to him the exchange rate of the dirhams in the murabahah (resale for profit), to suffice us from that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but when it is murabahah, inform him of that, and if it is musawamah (fixed price bargaining), there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْأَهْوَازِ: Ahwaz, a city in Iran used here as a trade location
key_terms.الْمُرَابَحَةِ: Murabahah, a trade contract where goods are sold at a profit margin over the cost
key_terms.مُسَاوَمَةً: Musawamah, a trade contract involving bargaining for a fixed price without necessarily disclosing cost

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disclosing exchange rates in trade transactions according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the transparency requirements in trade by distinguishing between fixed-profit sales (murabahah) and bargaining sales (musawamah). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) mandates that if the seller discloses the specific cost of currency exchange (sarf) incurred during the holding period, it must be revealed to the buyer in a murabahah context to ensure fairness, whereas in musawamah, such disclosure is optional. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preventing hidden riba (usury) or deception in commercial transactions involving fluctuating asset values.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Khalid Bin Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We send Dirhams to Ahwaz and there is an exchange rate for it, so the goods are bought for us with it. Then we wait. So when they are sold, the exchange rate is placed against it. So when we sell it, would it be upon us that we mention to him (the buyer) the exchange rate of the Dirham in the re-sale for a profit, to suffice us from that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but when it was the re-sale for a profit, so inform him with that, and if it was a fixed price, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdiy from Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Isma’il ibn ‘Abd al-Khaliq who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘We send dirham to Ahwaz where the price of dirham is different. With it goods are bought for us. We then wait until the goods are sold, the difference of price of dirham is deducted from it, if we sell. Is it necessary for us to mention the difference in prices in selling in the form of Murabahah (capital plus profit) on our part (of such difference)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, you must mention it if it is in the form of Murabahah (capital plus profit), but if it is in the form of Musawamah (fixed price regardless of capital) then it is lawful.’”
